questions.text: Which site-planning action is best supported for flora and fauna protection?

options.text: Retain or provide ecological corridors while minimizing vegetation clearing and alteration of drainage lines.
Clear vegetation first, then design the site around the remaining paved areas.
Treat habitat movement as a landscaping issue after building permit approval.
Use planting only for visual screening and exclude it from hazard planning.

questions.rationale: Retain or provide ecological corridors while minimizing vegetation clearing and alteration of drainage lines. This answer is supported by the checked local raw-source families for Flora and Fauna in Site Development.

questions.text: Which source-backed role can vegetation play in resilient site development?

options.text: Vegetation can support shade, stormwater control, erosion control, and habitat continuity.
Vegetation is limited to ornamental planting and has no climate-resilience role.
Vegetation should be removed near waterways to increase paved capacity.
Vegetation is relevant only inside buildings.

questions.rationale: Vegetation can support shade, stormwater control, erosion control, and habitat continuity. This answer is supported by the checked local raw-source families for Flora and Fauna in Site Development.
questions.explanation: The ECC is issued by DENR-EMB and must be obtained before the building permit application for any project in an ECA.

questions.text: What is the best exam reading of biodiversity areas in site planning?

options.text: Protected areas, key biodiversity areas, and critical habitats should be delineated and protected during land-use and site planning.
Biodiversity areas should be identified only after the structure is occupied.
Critical habitats are interchangeable with parking reserve areas.
Prime agricultural and heritage areas are outside planning review.

questions.rationale: Protected areas, key biodiversity areas, and critical habitats should be delineated and protected during land-use and site planning. This answer is supported by the checked local raw-source families for Flora and Fauna in Site Development.
